title: Start here: the five resources worth your first month
description: A deliberately short list. These five cover the fundamentals without redundancy, and each is free to read online. Work through them in order; the first two are the load-bearing ones.

items.note: The gentlest rigorous introduction. Read it cover to cover if you are new; the exercises are the point, not the prose.
Executable from first principles. Every concept here is implemented, which is the fastest way to find out whether you actually understood it.
The same material as ISLR with the mathematics kept in. Return to it once ISLR feels easy.
Reference rather than reading: use it to close specific gaps in linear algebra, probability and optimization as they appear.
The best-documented practical API in the field. Its user guide sections on model selection and preprocessing are worth reading independently of the library.

title: The transformer, from source to present
description: A reading trail in dependency order: the original architecture, a visual explanation, the two posts that make attention intuitive, the pretrained encoder that changed NLP, and the course that puts it all into practice.

items.note: Read Section 3 slowly. The scaling argument in 3.2 and the multi-head definition in 3.2.2 are the two things everything else builds on.
Read this first if the paper's tensor shapes are unclear; then go back to the paper.
The most complete single survey of attention variants, including the sub-quadratic families and their trade-offs.
Pre-transformer but essential: it shows what attention replaced, and why fixed-length context was the bottleneck.
The pretrain-then-fine-tune paradigm. Compare its bidirectional objective with the causal one in the original transformer.
Practical implementation with real code and checkpoints; the exercises make the theory concrete.

title: Why deep networks work: the theory shelf
description: Four references that treat deep learning as a mathematical object rather than an engineering recipe. These are dense; read them for the derivations, not for coverage.

items.note: Chapters 6, 8 and 9 are the core: feedforward networks, optimization, and sequence modelling.
Short and unusually clear. The residual identity path is the single most consequential architectural idea of the last decade.
Use it to check the probabilistic reading of any loss function you encounter.
Chapters 2-5 give the convex vocabulary that makes nonconvex results meaningful by contrast.

title: Reinforcement learning, properly
description: The canonical text plus three practical routes in. Reinforcement learning rewards patience: the theory chapter on temporal-difference learning is where most implementations either click or fail.

items.note: The definitive text. Chapters 3-6 (MDPs, dynamic programming, TD learning) are the foundation for everything after.
The best bridge from the textbook to working code, with honest notes about what does and does not transfer between environments.
Lecture notes and assignments from a full graduate course; the assignments are the value.
Keep open for the probability and concentration results used in regret and policy-gradient bounds.

title: Computer vision: lectures and lineage
description: Stanford's lecture notes for the fundamentals, then the two papers that define the modern architectural lineage.

items.note: The convolutional network notes remain the clearest derivation of backpropagation through a conv layer.
Read for the identity path and for the depth experiment that motivated it.
Chapter 9 for the convolution algebra and parameter-sharing argument.
The vision and autograd references; use the documentation as the authority on tensor semantics rather than blog posts.
